title: Council approves late-night bus route 91 return
subtitle: Also: plan to end chronic homelessness, Bleams Road tender, 2024 tax ratios, Ayr truck study, Wilmot land delegation.
overview: Regional Council voted to bring back the route 91 Late Night Loop on Thursday to Saturday nights before September 2, 2024 {{vote:m15}}. It also directed Grand River Transit to include routes 91 and 92, or equivalent night service, in its 2025 business plan and to treat night transit extensions as 2025 budget items. About 17 delegates, mostly students, spoke in support. Staff estimated route 91 would cost about $61,000 a year, and the 2024 portion has no funding source yet.

Council accepted the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness in principle {{vote:m5}}, with area municipalities to join the co-creators group and a detailed plan due in the 2025 budget process. It also set 2024 property tax ratios, accepted a $20,071,877 tender for Bleams Road improvements in Kitchener, and asked staff to explore non-profit leases for two properties to provide culturally responsive childcare.

Council also heard a late delegation from Wilmot farmers about the land assembly there. It was not an agenda item, but council agreed to hear it. After adjourning from open session, council went into closed session on a proposed land acquisition.

decisions.detail: Council directed GRT to temporarily reinstate the route 91 Late Night Loop on Thursday to Saturday before September 2, 2024, and to include night transit in the 2025 business plan and budget.

Council accepted the plan in principle as the official homelessness plan and directed staff to add area municipalities to the co-creators group and return with a detailed funding and advocacy plan in the 2025 budget process.

Council directed staff to explore leasing 30 Christopher Drive in Cambridge and 104 Stirling Avenue South in Kitchener to non-profits for culturally responsive childcare for Indigenous and other families facing systemic barriers.

Council accepted the T. Musselman Excavating Limited tender of $20,071,877 plus taxes for Regional Road 56 work between Fischer-Hallman Road and Trussler Road, and approved a $1,822,400 gross, $0 net cost increase for work done for the City of Kitchener.

Council set the 2024 property class tax ratios, received the 2023 Plan Update, and approved the 2025 budget review timetable with all Strategic Plan and Budget Committee meetings starting at 9:00 a.m.

decisions.item: Planning and Works summary of April 9
decisions.detail: Council approved phased payments of the Roger Street tax increment grant, expropriation steps for the Roseville Road and Edworthy Side Road intersection, extending the 50 km/h limit on Swan Street, and a revised storm sewer cost sharing policy.

decisions.item: MobilityPLUS and Ayr truck route study
decisions.detail: Council assigned a new project manager to speed up MobilityPLUS scheduling software updates, and directed a study of truck issues in downtown Ayr along with interim measures such as signage and speed reductions.

debate: Delegates argued the bus service stops at midnight even though students pay for a transit pass in tuition. They said that leaves walking late at night or paying for a ride share, which raises safety and affordability concerns. They also noted night shift workers and late GO bus arrivals with no connecting local service.

Some councillors raised equity. They said Cambridge and other areas lack comparable service and asked whether other parts of the region, such as industrial areas with night shifts, should be assessed first. Supporters answered that this restores a past service in a dense area and that need should guide priorities. Delegates said it could be a pilot that informs wider night service.

Staff said routes 91 and 92 were cancelled in 2019 for low ridership and that current demand is unknown. Staff said route 91 would cost roughly $61,000 a year and the 2024 portion is unfunded. A full overnight network would need major operating changes, such as 24-hour maintenance and cleaning and updated labour agreements. Reinstating only route 91 would need minimal changes.

Council first considered referring the motion to staff for more information, and one councillor suggested deferral. After a floor amendment, council narrowed the immediate step to route 91 and kept the 2025 business plan and budget direction. One councillor asked that the equity review of other areas still go ahead.

One councillor asked that any extended conventional service be matched by MobilityPLUS, as accessible rides late at night are hard to get. Staff agreed and said it would be added to the tracking list.
